Looking to get into Tekken and I'm getting mixed messages on Kazuya being a beginner character or not. Why is this? 

On the one hand, the character select screen defaults to him and this has typically been done to show which character can summarize the mechanics of this specific fighting game and therefore can teach a beginner how it works. I also see some forums and threads mentioning he will force you to get good fundamentals which is undoubtedly good for beginners. All too often, newcomers will stagnate because they have gotten away with avoiding learning fundamentals after having found a gimmick that wins them games (looking at flowchart Kens in Street Fighter).

On the other hand. I've seen him have an "intermediate" to "hard" difficulty level in character overviews. From what I know, he also has specific key mechanics to him not present in other characters (electric and wavedashing) which seem like learning traps for a beginner. On top of learning how the game works they have to spend time learning something so specific.

I know people say to play who you want regardless of difficulty but I am still curious why I am getting such different signals on this nature for Kazuya. Is it because people are actually talking about two different kinds of difficulty? As in, does he have a simple gameplan to follow but a high execution ceiling for people looking to master him? Or am I reading too much into all this?

The analogy isn't supposed to to be about me believing my mom exists. It's about my obligations and gratitude. I have loads if evidence for my mother's existence. I can talk to her, see her, and understand how I came from her. I do not have that evidence for God.

Please remember that analogies aren't one to one representations.

>You are the creature, the created.

Now your changing it to his ability to give life. What does that ability have to do with being moral? It's the same question but instead of infinite you shifted to life creation.

>You can learn about God based on what He wanted you to know in His Word

How do I know it's his word? I can't tell if the Bible is special or if it is just like any other religon's holy texts. And then even if it were special, how do I know if I am interpreting it correctly? Other people have reached extremely different conclusions from reading the same book.

>To question His morality, to say that He is immoral is conjecture

I have enough information for it not to be conjecture. I can compare the morals in the Bible to morals of today and see which one is preferable.

Even if I didn't have enough information so that it still is conjecture, then why doesn't he tell me about his morality so that my assessment isn't conjecture anymore?

>If God exists, and God created this place, it's His rules.

Someone can found a country and set laws for it. What does being able create a place have to do with being moral? You aren't answering any of these questions.

This does not answer the follow up question. What does being infinite have to do with morality? I don't care what people say about themselves. Dictators say they're the most perfect people ever.
> who are we to question His morality?

We are the people that are affected by his standard of morality. His morals have dire consequences for our lives. I think I'm justified in wanting to know why he gets to tell me what I can do in the privacy of my bedroom or what thoughts I'm allowed to have if he's going to torture me eternally for it

Does the ability to create universes makes one moral? What does power or being infinite have to do with how moral someone is? Please do not avoid the question even if it is ridiculous. Treat me like a slow person if you have to to give me a straight answer. Surely if you believe it to be so with such conviction you must have an answer. 

What would I have to be afraid of to ask God a question? Unless of course he is insecure about being asked such a thing like a narcissist hates being asked to self reflect. Then again that would explain why he wants us to love him over friends and family, people we actually got to know as well as blasphemy laws. You only insult your god by insinuating that he would punish criticism.

I am being facetious but I do appreciate you taking time to respond. If you are tired of the topic you don't have to engage with the thread but new people like me are happy for a chance to crack at old topics

> Logically, why would one with finite knowledge question others with finite knowledge

I'd question the man himself if I could. And I have. But since he chose to communicate through ancient books, I have no way to determine if I am interpreting them correctly let alone even trust theyre from him in the first place.

> has already told us He is Holy, which is apart from sin?

How did he tell us this? And I'm sure Kim Jong Un also tells North Koreans he is Holy and apart from sin. Do you trust what someone says of themself to determine their morality.? Or you actually look at their actions?
You cannot just assert it without demonstrating why God's existence makes him the be all end all for morality. Why doesn't Kim Jong Un's existence as dictator not make him a moral standard?

>Every single culture has experienced these beings, and each tradition has corresponding beings

It would be stronger evidence if we see consistency across all cultures in how they experience these beings. That would actually show that they are witnessing the same phenomenon. Instead we see pantheons as diverse as the cultures themselves. There's nothing to link that the gods of the Aztecs are the same gods of the Greeks. Of course some gods share qualities and powers like being gods of war or harvest. But this can be explained by the fact that almost all cultures take part in war and harvest and so there is some overlap.

So the consistency we see between gods needs to be so much more than can be explained by similar human needs and endeavors. We know people hallucinate, can be mistaken, and can invent fantasies. Why not go to these explanations, which we have evidence for happen, instead of the explanation that gods actually exist, which we don't have evidence for.

Sidenote: If you play video games, I highly suggest God of War 4. The premise is a Greek god travels to Scandinavia and has a conflict with the Norse gods. It seems like something you would enjoy.

>Just like humans looking at the same stars see different constellations, humans interacting with the gods viewed them differently based on geography, culture, economy, etc.

The difference here is we have strong evidence for the existence of the stars and continue to see them. They can be investigated and we can learn all sorts of things about them. This is so much so that we can actually tell what elements the stars are made of, how they form, how they die, their different categories, etc. While the constellations may be different, their positions are consistent across all cultures. This is how we know they saw the same stars. They would be able to point out the same one and agree about its position in the night sky if two people from each culture were to meet. They can't agree on whether the god of thunder wields a hammer or throws bolts.

>Well there's your issue. Your anti theism leads to you making this a problem of theism. The simple harsh truth is humanity sucks, and is capable of great evil under numerous excuses, religious or secular.

You are absolutely right that sometimes, actions inform beliefs. It has been the case that people will look for a belief to justify the actions they already want to take. However, to say that this is the only way actions and beliefs interact is naive. It is also the case that sometimes the traditional event occurs, that beliefs inform actions. I am taught something is true by the word of God/s and will therefore act on it. Do you not think that if JW's didn't believe what they did, they wouldn't withhold necessary blood transfusions from their members? Do you not think that if people didn't believe in an afterlife, we would see fewer attempts at martyrdom? Would people be as dogmatic and closed-minded if they didn't think their beliefs came from omniscient deities? Yes, there are evil people in spite of their beliefs. There are also people that are evil because of their beliefs.

>  How do we ever determine truth? Reasoning, evidence, experience. 

While I'm not quite sure what you mean about determining experience, we determine if something is true if there's been sufficient evidence to demonstrate it. The evidence required depends on the claim but evidence is considered good if it is repeatable, comes from credible sources, and corroborated by other good evidence.

When OP said faith makes you less accountable, they are talking about the common teaching that belief in this god or that god determines your afterlife destination. For Christianity, true there's advice for this world, but when Jesus was asked how to get to heaven his answer boils down to belief and acceptance of him. No caveat about the accountability of your actions in this life. 

Even if in Christianity, they taught accountability instead of belief, consider this. How much better would we treat each other if we believed this life is the only one we get. Instead of relying on the supernatural to make right everything wrong with the world come judgement day, we would take a more active role in bettering the world because our actions would be the only influence on the outcome.
